what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1990?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 2010 report (calendar wages) and FY2011-FY2025 (fiscal). The 1990 annual town report (76 pages) prints no wage list: its whole text was searched for wage, gross and earning, and the only hits are prose (p13 the drug-officer grant `to pay for wages`, p27 the Treasurer on staff hours, p21 `ACCRUED WAGES PAYABLE` on the balance sheet) and a licence line (p14). — closes: the Town's calendar-1990 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in fiscal 1991?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1990 report records the vote but not the schedule: p44 Article 5 votes `the Classification & Salary Schedule proposed by the Personnel Committee and appearing in the Report of the Finance Committee`, and no schedule is printed anywhere in the 76 pages (searched: classification, salary schedule). — closes: the Finance Committee's report to the May 12, 1990 Annual Town Meeting, which printed the Classification & Salary Schedule.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in fiscal 1990?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1990 annual town report prints no special revenue schedule: the whole text was searched for special revenue, revolving and enterprise, and the only special revenue figure is the one column of the combined balance sheet (p21: cash $179,577, total fund equity $175,034). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1990 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in fiscal 1990?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1990 report prints none: the balance sheet carries a capital projects column holding only $1,379 (p21), and the text was searched for capital project, capital plan and capital improvement (the only hit is p10, the Planning Board naming a Capital Improvement Planning Committee). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1990 capital projects fund ledger.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY1991 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1990 report prints no capital plan; p10 says only that the Planning Board is `participating with the Capital Improvement Planning Committee and the Accountant's office on a Town-wide inventory`. — closes: that Committee's inventory or the Finance Committee's FY1991 report listing capital articles.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 1990 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 1990 report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (pp29-31) and no debt-limit statement: debt limit and outstanding debt were searched across all 76 pages and the index (p73) and do not appear. — closes: the Town's FY1990 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for fiscal 1991?
why: `report-valuation` holds the Assessors' tables (assessments by class, valuation and tax history, overlay, new growth) from the 2001 and 2010 reports. The 1990 report prints a valuation only as two lines in the ABOUT THE TOWN table (p3: real estate $557,346,832, personal property $12,123,493, tax rate $10.92 for fiscal 1991) and the Assessors' report (p8) is prose on exemptions and revaluation with no class table. — closes: the Assessors' FY1991 tax rate recapitulation filed with the Department of Revenue.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1990, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1990 report prints only a paragraph (p17): `twenty-two visits were made to Town businesses with a total of $687.00 collected in fees`; the receipts page (p22) prints SEALING FEES $531.00, and the two figures are not reconciled on either page. — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1990 annual report to the Division of Standards.

what: What did the town take in from state revenue, line by line, in fiscal 1990?
why: `annual-report-receipts` holds every receipt line the receipts page prints. The 1990 receipts page (p22, printed page 20) is cut off at the bottom: its STATE REVENUE section ends at ABATEMENTS ELDERLY $34,710.00 while the summary on the same page prints STATE REVENUE $1,555,317.75, and the 125 receipt lines read sum to $7,193,802.84 against the printed GRAND TOTAL $8,174,269.84, short by $980,467.00. The next page (p23, printed page 21) is the appropriations schedule, so the missing lines are not on the following page; whether the scan or the printing dropped them is not established. — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1990 receipts ledger or a clean copy of the 1990 report's printed page 20.
